comparable.e2e_consumer: client/E2eLatency.java, compiled by client/Dockerfile against the Kafka image's kafka-clients and run by that image's JVM: assign, seek to the end, latency = poll() return time minus the record's CreateTime, 1 ms buckets

kafka_profiles.defaults: Kafka as shipped: log.flush.interval.messages unset, so an acknowledgement does not wait for an fsync
kafka_profiles.fsync-parity: flush.messages=1 on every broker and on the topic: every append is flushed before it is acknowledged

configs.kafka_compose:
# Apache Kafka for the head-to-head comparison (#595, #596): three brokers in
# KRaft mode, each a combined broker+controller, RF=3, min.insync.replicas=2.
#
# Fairness rule 1: every broker gets EXACTLY the limits each VTOP node gets in
# compose.vtop.yml (2 CPUs, 2 GiB, no swap, a named volume on the same Docker
# VM disk). Change one file, change the other; run.py records both in
# environment.json and refuses to start when they differ.
#
# Everything else is Kafka as shipped (profile `defaults`, #595 rule 4): no
# flush.messages, so a broker acknowledges on replication, not on fsync.
#
# The image is pinned by tag AND digest (rule 8); KAFKA_IMAGE overrides both.
name: kc-kafka

x-broker: &broker
  image: ${KAFKA_IMAGE:-apache/kafka:4.3.2@sha256:852a0d49fc4e656b022e7f23785411802c9a088c78a7c5e39f33969de9c227a7}
  cpus: 2
  mem_limit: 2g
  memswap_limit: 2g
  ulimits:
    nofile: { soft: 65536, hard: 65536 }
  # The same hardening as the VTOP nodes (fairness rule 1): no capabilities
  # (the broker listens above 1024 as appuser), no setuid gain. Not
  # read_only or pids_limit: the first would move the JVM's writable paths
  # to tmpfs, the second caps its threads; either could change what is
  # measured.
  cap_drop: [ALL]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  networks: [bench]
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "/opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 > /dev/null 2>&1"]
    interval: 5s
    timeout: 20s
    retries: 30
    start_period: 10s

x-env: &env
  # One fixed id: KRaft formats every log dir with it on first start.
  CLUSTER_ID: "a2NvbXBhcmUtcGhhc2UtMQ"
  KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: "broker,controller"
  KAFKA_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093"
  KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: "CONTROLLER"
  KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: "PLAINTEXT"
  KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: "CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT"
  KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: "1@kafka-1:9093,2@kafka-2:9093,3@kafka-3:9093"
  KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: "/var/lib/kafka/data"
  # The replication contract (#595 rule 3).
  KAFKA_DEFAULT_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_MIN_INSYNC_REPLICAS: "2"
  KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: "2"
  # The benchmark topic is created explicitly by run.py with these settings;
  # a typo'd topic must not be auto-created with others.
  KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: "false"

services:
  kafka-1:
    <<: *broker
    hostname: kafka-1
    environment:
      <<: *env
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "1"
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://kafka-1:9092"
    volumes: ["kafka-1-data:/var/lib/kafka/data"]
  kafka-2:
    <<: *broker
    hostname: kafka-2
    environment:
      <<: *env
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "2"
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://kafka-2:9092"
    volumes: ["kafka-2-data:/var/lib/kafka/data"]
  kafka-3:
    <<: *broker
    hostname: kafka-3
    environment:
      <<: *env
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "3"
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://kafka-3:9092"
    volumes: ["kafka-3-data:/var/lib/kafka/data"]

volumes:
  kafka-1-data:
  kafka-2-data:
  kafka-3-data:

networks:
  bench:
    name: kc-kafka-bench
configs.vtop_compose:
# VTOP for the head-to-head comparison (#595, #596): three data nodes from the
# image docker/Dockerfile builds, one range replicated to all three with a
# write quorum of 2 of 3, and the Kafka gateway on the range's leader.
#
# Fairness rule 1: EXACTLY the per-node limits compose.kafka.yml gives each
# Kafka broker (2 CPUs, 2 GiB, no swap, a named volume on the same Docker VM
# disk). run.py records both in environment.json and refuses to start when
# they differ.
#
# VTOP_IMAGE is set by run.py to the image it built from the commit under
# test (vtop-bench:<sha>), so the recorded commit is the one that ran.
name: kc-vtop

x-node: &node
  image: ${VTOP_IMAGE:?set VTOP_IMAGE to the vtop-bench image run.py built}
  entrypoint: ["vtop-node", "data", "--config", "/etc/vtop/node.yaml"]
  cpus: 2
  mem_limit: 2g
  memswap_limit: 2g
  ulimits:
    nofile: { soft: 65536, hard: 65536 }
  # The same hardening as compose.kafka.yml's brokers (fairness rule 1): no
  # capabilities (the node listens above 1024 as user vtop), no setuid gain.
  # Not read_only or pids_limit: the first would move writable paths to
  # tmpfs, the second caps threads; either could change what is measured.
  cap_drop: [ALL]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  networks: [bench]
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:9600/readyz > /dev/null"]
    interval: 2s
    timeout: 5s
    retries: 60
    start_period: 2s

services:
  # Followers first: the leader's quorum needs them listening.
  vtop-2:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-2
    volumes:
      - "./vtop/follower-1.yaml:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      # Mounted at the image's home (owned by the unprivileged `vtop` user), so
      # a fresh named volume inherits that ownership.
      - "vtop-2-data:/home/vtop"
  vtop-3:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-3
    volumes:
      - "./vtop/follower-2.yaml:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      - "vtop-3-data:/home/vtop"
  vtop-1:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-1
    depends_on:
      vtop-2: { condition: service_healthy }
      vtop-3: { condition: service_healthy }
    volumes:
      # ${VTOP_LEADER_CONFIG} names another leader file: run.py's per-run group-commit config (#752) or crash.py's
      # group-commit configurations (#599); unset, it is the shipped one.
      - "${VTOP_LEADER_CONFIG:-./vtop/leader.yaml}:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      - "vtop-1-data:/home/vtop"

volumes:
  vtop-1-data:
  vtop-2-data:
  vtop-3-data:

networks:
  bench:
    name: kc-vtop-bench

configs.vtop_leader:
# VTOP node 1: the range's static leader, with the Kafka gateway (#225).
#
# The shape scripts/live-chaos scenario 17 drives with a stock librdkafka
# client (a static leader at a fixed fencing epoch, two followers, quorum
# acknowledgement), moved into containers. Plaintext planes, as Kafka's
# PLAINTEXT listeners on the other side, so neither system pays for TLS; the
# `-on-any-interface` spelling is the node's own opt-in for leaving loopback.
#
# Every engine knob not written here is the binary's default (profile
# `defaults`, #595 rule 4): the gateway appends with Durability::Quorum, which
# acknowledges after a majority of the three replicas (leader included) has
# made the append locally durable (fsync) — 2 of 3, the write quorum the
# comparison asks for. Kafka under `defaults` acknowledges on replication
# without fsync; that difference is stated in the report, never hidden.
role: leader
node_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1
cluster_id: 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
data_dir: /home/vtop/data
fencing_epoch: 18
range: { topic: "bench", topic_epoch: 1, range_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1, range_generation: 0 }
segment_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000d1
native_listen: "0.0.0.0:9400"
replica_listen: "0.0.0.0:9300"
followers:
  - { node_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a2, addr: "vtop-2:9300", server_name: "vtop-2" }
  - { node_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a3, addr: "vtop-3:9300", server_name: "vtop-3" }
replica_transport: plaintext-on-any-interface
native_transport: plaintext-on-any-interface
principal_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ce
observability: { listen: "0.0.0.0:9600" }
kafka:
  # Off loopback because the client runs in its own container; the gateway
  # demands that be said by name (`any_interface`), and Metadata must name a
  # host the client container resolves (`advertised_host`).
  listen: "0.0.0.0:9092"
  any_interface: true
  advertised_host: "vtop-1"
  advertised_port: 9092
  topic: "bench"
  node_id: 1
